84: 4.8. How do you manage customers with high seasonality?

Typical, reasonable daily volume fluctuations are inherent to most businesses and are addressed as part of our labor staffing strategy. CEVA’s approach to hourly labor is to employ full-time associates for stable/minimum volumes and utilize temporary personnel for any volatile volume fluctuations. Temporary staff is typically scheduled for less than 40 hours per week so that additional hours are available for routine volume fluctuations.  
 
Requirements beyond that are satisfied by either adding to the temporary pool and/or seeking additional resources from other CEVA locations with bandwidth capacity.  Depending on the duration of the burst/spike, temporary shift changes may also be implemented (staffing a second or third shift, extending shift hours to 10 hours per day, etc.).  
 
Management resource alternatives are also directly impacted by the magnitude and duration of the occurrence. The primary sources of assistance include corporate support staff, subject matter experts (SMEs), logistics engineering resources, as well as management from other CEVA facilities that have the bandwidth to support the event.
 
We expect our clients to provide a forecast for Black Friday and other peak periods. The account team will work closely with your team to plan additional staffing to accommodate the expected volumes. Temporary staff will be onboarded and trained in a clearly defined ramp-up schedule in partnership with our temporary agencies. Shifts will be added to ensure orders are shipped as per agreed upon peak period SLA’s. If needed, additional MHE will also be rented during the peak period.

90: 5.1. Please describe your business continuity plan in case of any incident with your Company:

CEVA has an obligation to our customers to be as prepared as possible to reduce the effect of potential disasters or accidents. Therefore, CEVA’s approach to disaster recovery is to provide redundancy for critical components and links to prevent outages and to establish detailed procedures in the event that an outage occurs. These procedures include standardized responses to various potential natural disasters and systems failures that could affect our ability to support our customer.  In our contingency planning for disaster recovery, CEVA determines the required actions in response to varying degrees of service interruption caused by either an act of nature, accident, loss of power, or loss of an element of the system.  
The defined output for any such disaster or power outage is documented in the Disaster Recovery Plan.  

This plan is a living document that minimally provides the following information:
- A notification roster that lists contact information in an escalation format.
- Procedures for surviving a natural disaster, such as a fire or tornado, that outline general information, escape routes, employee muster procedures, rescue and medical responsibilities, and a preferred method for reporting the disaster.
- Procedures for addressing how power outages are addressed that include the use of either an uninterruptible power supply (UPS) or back-up generator designated to provide continuous power to identified critical systems and maintain our ability to process and move freight, including contact and other required information should the back-up power supplies fail.
- Procedures for addressing system failures that include what to do and who to call for any system failure including RF, server, communications, PC, printer, software, and other failures.

Additionally, CEVA’s standard operating procedures (SOPs) require each contracted business operation to fully develop, document, and maintain a potential problem analysis (PPA) specific to the services provided. The PPA includes responsibility assignments, notification and employee rosters, a versatility matrix, key vendor/subcontractor contact information, and most likely problem scenarios with recommended solutions for issues, such as operational crises, natural disasters, and workforce disruptions.  The document is prepared during implementation and is updated and maintained by CEVA management.  
 
Regarding our systems, we provide onsite redundancy consisting of the equipment located within our Culpepper (USCD) and Ashburn (USAD) Data Centers to automatically recover from system, network, and application failures. Recovery occurs in seconds, requiring minimal manual intervention, resulting in minimal user-impact.
 
Onsite back-up systems include redundant servers, storage systems, routers, network connections, power supplies, and power sources. Because most outages result from a software or infrastructure failure, real-time, automated recovery of on-site systems provide the foundation for high-availability. Application data is protected through automated daily back-ups based on application recovery requirements. Copies of the back-up media are stored off-site in fully protected tape vaults and are cycled daily.  Back-up media that display a failure, or are more than two years old, are removed from the process and destroyed.

Kuehne + Nagel's general Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery Plan is part of KN's standard solution scope.  The plan serves as a guideline to KN offices and operations worldwide to formulate location-specific procedures to prevent and minimize the effect of possible disasters. A detailed description of adequate responses in case of a disaster or emergency are included in the formal plan.  The plan consists of three major components:

1.  Risk Management and Disaster Prevention - This includes the assessment of possible risks that may affect Kuehne + Nagel's or its customers' business and consequently result in preventative actions aimed as minimizing possible risks.
2.  Effective Emergency Response Actions - In case of a disaster, emergency or serious incident, effective emergency response actions to be taken are described.
3. Guarantee Continuity of Operations - In case a disaster or incident could not be adequately prevented, the main objectives of the recovery process are to ensure emergency processes and methodologies are in place to allow continuous client support in the event of any disaster.
